text:
elaine: Quick sync — I'm drafting the Dedicated Capacity PRD. Need to lock: SLA targets, what we can cut for launch, and autoscale behavior for noisy tenants. TL;DR: customers want predictable p95 and guaranteed throughput for reserved pools.

matt: +1. Can we set a single clear SLO for launch instead of multiple brittle targets? e.g., p95 latency <= 150ms for 512 token requests at committed throughput.

sophie: That feels reasonable. We should call out degraded behavior when burst > commitment — how we surface it to customers and whether we throttle or queue.

elaine: Proposal in PRD: 3-tier behavior. 1) Within commitment: hard SLO, priority traffic. 2) Soft burst: best-effort with queueing and 99% availability target. 3) Over-burst: shed to cheaper hosted fallback model with graceful degr. Need buy-in on fallback and billing semantics.

ron: Important: fallback must preserve privacy guarantees for Private customers. For Dedicated customers w/ reserved pools, fallback to hosted is only allowed if they opt in. Add opt-in flag in contract and API.

alex: Agreed. Also, we need explicit autoscale cooldowns to avoid thrash. My suggestion: scale-up immediate up to N nodes (burst capacity), scale-down after 10m of low utilization, with one emergency failover path to the regional pool.

matt: Will the autoscaler consider KV-cache warmup times? Scaling from 0 -> N adds cold-start token latency that breaks the SLO. We should define cache-warm profiles and minimum standby to avoid that for committed throughput.

elaine: Good catch. Add acceptance criteria: cold-start p95 for first token <= 500ms for scale-from-0, but for committed throughput we require warm pool with p95 <= 150ms. Also add requirement: autoscaler must pre-warm KV caches when scaling predicted load > 50% of current capacity.

ron: From legal/commercial POV, we need to show how refunds/credits work when we miss the committed SLO. Propose: standard credit schedule (see snippet in PRD) and a post-mortem / remediation plan.

sophie: On throughput sizing: we need a sizing formula in PRD: committed_tps = max(peak_tps_95, requested_min_commit) and include token-length assumptions per workload class. Engineers: can you add measurable benchmarks?

alex: I'll attach a bench matrix. For initial launch we size for 10k tokens/sec sustained per pool for the smallest reserved tier. Bench numbers: 512 tokens/generation, batch size ~4, GPU type A100-40 => ~250 tok/s per GPU (example). We'll include fudge factor 0.7 for headroom.

elaine: Acceptance criteria (draft in PRD) — must pass before GA: 
```
- Load test: sustained committed throughput for 30m at requested token size with observed p95 latency <= 150ms
- Failover test: simulate a node failure, failover recovery time <= 60s, no more than 3% error rate spike
- Burst test: submit bursts 2x committed for 10m; system must honor soft-burst policy and not exceed 5% error rate
- Billing/opt-in: fallback to hosted must be explicit in account settings and documented
```

matt: Need to define observability signals and dashboards for customers: token-level cost, per-route latency, queue-length, number of pre-warmed nodes, and autoscale decisions. Also an API endpoint /reserved/status that gives current mode (within-commit, soft-burst, degraded).

elaine: Agreed. We'll add requirements for trace correlation and a customer-facing incident timeline when we drop below SLO.

ron: Edge cases: sustained small requests (10 tokens) vs large batched requests (2k tokens). Must enforce per-request token caps per pool to avoid single huge request consuming the pool. Add a per-request max_token configurable in the contract.

sophie: Also consider cold-cache hot-spotting: one tenant sends many new prefixes and causes cache churn. We should document eviction policy and an optional per-tenant cache quota.

alex: For launch cuts: recommend shipping without per-tenant cache quotas (complex), but include per-request token cap and fallback + throttling. We can iterate cache quotas in Q2.

elaine: Sounds pragmatic. Final checklist for PRD to ship: SLA numbers, autoscale policy (up/down thresholds, cooldowns, pre-warm), fallback opt-in and billing semantics, acceptance test definitions, observability dashboard list, contract flags (max_token, fallback_opt_in).

matt: +1 from me. One more ask: define negative test for graceful degradation — e.g., ensure model outputs truncated gracefully when fallback with different model size. Need automated assertion that responses still match schema and provide degrade_reason header.

elaine: I'll add that to acceptance tests. Anyone object to this plan? If not, I'll update PRD and tag eng-runtime + sales for pricing language.

ron: No objections. Please ping legal for fallback consent wording.

sophie: No objections. I'll review the PRD for edge-case wording.

alex: I'll add bench results and a preliminary autoscaler config snippet.

deploy-bot: deploy-note: PRD draft updated by elaine in /docs/prd/dedicated-capacity/ (link) :thumbsup:

elaine: Thanks team — I'll push the draft in the next hour and request reviews from eng-runtime, sales, and legal.
